sub: Michigan Motor Vehicle Financial Responsibility Law
q: A Michigan auto policy is issued on August 1, 2026. The named insured never completes a form choosing bodily injury liability limits. Under the Michigan Insurance Code, what bodily injury limits apply?
choices: $20,000 per person / $40,000 per accident
$50,000 per person / $100,000 per accident
$100,000 per person / $300,000 per accident
$250,000 per person / $500,000 per accident
explain: After July 1, 2020, MCL 500.3009(1) requires 250/500, and 3009(8) applies those limits when no effective lower-limit choice is made. 20/40 applied only before July 2, 2020, and 50/100 is the lowest limit that can be elected.

sub: Michigan Motor Vehicle Financial Responsibility Law
q: For a Michigan auto policy issued after July 1, 2020, what is the lowest bodily injury liability limit the Michigan Insurance Code lets a named insured choose, and how is it chosen?
choices: $20,000/$40,000, by verbal request to the agent
$25,000/$50,000, by written notice to the Secretary of State
$50,000/$100,000, by completing and signing a DIFS form
$50,000/$100,000, with no form needed once premium is paid
explain: MCL 500.3009(5) allows limits lower than 250/500, but not below 50/100. The person must complete the DIFS form, delivered and signed as section 3107e provides.

sub: Michigan Motor Vehicle Financial Responsibility Law
q: What is the minimum property damage liability limit the Michigan Insurance Code requires on a Michigan auto liability policy?
explain: Section 3009(1)(c) requires at least $10,000 for property of others. DIFS describes it as covering damage your vehicle does to property in another state. In Michigan, PPI (up to $1 million) pays for damage to others' property such as buildings, fences and properly parked vehicles, but not moving or improperly parked vehicles or their contents, and tort liability for property damage is largely abolished. $3,000 is the mini-tort amount (accidents after July 1, 2020) for vehicle damage not covered by insurance.

sub: Michigan Motor Vehicle Financial Responsibility Law
q: Maria's auto policy lists her 19-year-old son as a named excluded driver. He crashes Maria's car while driving it. Under Michigan law, which statement is correct?
choices: Liability coverage applies, but only up to the minimum limits
Liability coverage applies, but PIP is excluded for passengers
Liability coverage applies in full, and he is entitled to PIP benefits
All liability coverage is void, and he is not entitled to PIP benefits
explain: A named-driver exclusion under 3009(2) carries the required warning that when the excluded person operates a vehicle, all liability coverage is void and no one is insured. Section 3113(d) bars PIP for a person operating a vehicle as a named excluded operator.

sub: Michigan Motor Vehicle Financial Responsibility Law
q: Under the Michigan Vehicle Code, an owner or operator who fails to produce evidence of insurance when a police officer requests it is responsible for:
choices: A 2-year license revocation
A misdemeanor punishable by up to 1 year in jail and a $1,000 fine
A civil infraction
A felony
explain: Failing to produce proof (or to have insurance) is a civil infraction under 257.328(1). The 1-year/$1,000 misdemeanor in 257.328(6) is for KNOWINGLY producing false evidence of insurance.

sub: Michigan Motor Vehicle Financial Responsibility Law
q: Under the Michigan Vehicle Code, while a transportation network company (ride-share) driver is engaged in a prearranged ride, the required residual liability coverage is at least:
choices: $50,000/$100,000 bodily injury and $25,000 property damage
$250,000/$500,000 bodily injury and $10,000 property damage
$500,000 combined single limit
$1,000,000 combined single limit
explain: Section 257.518b(1)(b) requires a $1,000,000 CSL (plus PIP and PPI) during a prearranged ride. 50/100/25 applies while the driver is logged on and available but not yet on a ride.

sub: Michigan Motor Vehicle Financial Responsibility Law
q: Michigan's no-fault law requires the owner or registrant of a motor vehicle required to be registered in Michigan to maintain all of the following EXCEPT:
choices: Collision coverage
Personal protection insurance (PIP)
Property protection insurance (PPI)
Residual liability insurance
explain: Required security is PIP, PPI and residual liability (3101(1)). Collision is optional, though insurers must offer Michigan's collision options (3037).

sub: Michigan Motor Vehicle Financial Responsibility Law
q: Michigan's no-fault law treats a person who rents or leases a car as an "owner" when the rental or use is for a period greater than:
choices: 10 days
30 days
60 days
6 months
explain: Section 3101(3)(l)(i) defines owner to include a person renting a motor vehicle, or having its use under a lease or otherwise, for more than 30 days.

sub: Michigan Motor Vehicle Financial Responsibility Law
q: Under Michigan's no-fault law, a nonresident whose car is not registered in Michigan may operate it in Michigan without Michigan no-fault security for no more than:
choices: 10 consecutive days
An aggregate of 30 days in any calendar year
An aggregate of 60 days in any calendar year
An aggregate of 90 days in any 12-month period
explain: Under 3102(1), a nonresident may not operate the vehicle in Michigan for an aggregate of more than 30 days in any calendar year without maintaining security.

sub: Michigan Motor Vehicle Financial Responsibility Law
q: What penalty does Michigan's no-fault law set for an owner who operates a motor vehicle on a Michigan highway without the required no-fault security?
choices: No penalty, if the driver holds a valid Michigan driver's license
A civil infraction with a court fee of no more than $25
A misdemeanor: a $200 to $500 fine, up to 1 year in jail, or both
A felony: up to 5 years in prison, a $5,000 fine, or both
explain: Section 3102(2) makes it a misdemeanor for the owner or registrant, and for anyone who knowingly drives an uninsured vehicle, punishable by a $200–$500 fine, up to 1 year in jail, or both.

q: Michigan law established the Michigan Automobile Insurance Placement Facility primarily to:
choices: Investigate and prosecute auto insurance fraud
Reimburse member insurers for PIP losses above the catastrophic claims retention
Set uniform rates for all private passenger auto insurers in Michigan
Guarantee auto insurance to people unable to get it through ordinary methods
explain: Under 3301, every insurer authorized to write auto insurance in Michigan must take part, to guarantee availability and to preserve price competition. Reimbursing catastrophic PIP losses is the MCCA's job (3104).

q: Under Michigan law, how often must a designated participating member notify people insured through the Michigan Automobile Insurance Placement Facility of the statutory eligibility standards for buying auto insurance in the voluntary market?
choices: At least once each year
Only when the insured asks for reassignment
Once every 3 years
Only when the original application is taken
explain: Section 3365(3) requires each designated participating member to give this notice at least once each year, on a commissioner-approved form.

q: Under Michigan's no-fault law, PIP allowable expenses do NOT include:
choices: Hospital room charges above the semiprivate rate when special or intensive care is not needed
Reasonably necessary accommodations for the injured person's care, recovery, or rehabilitation
Reasonably necessary medical products and services for the injured person's care
Reasonable charges for the injured person's rehabilitation and recovery
explain: Section 3107(1)(a)(i) excludes hospital room charges above a reasonable and customary semiprivate charge, unless special or intensive care is required.

q: Under Michigan's no-fault law, PIP pays funeral and burial expenses up to the amount stated in the policy, which must be:
choices: At least $1,000 and no more than $3,000
At least $1,750 and no more than $5,000
Exactly $5,000
Unlimited, subject only to reasonableness
explain: Section 3107(1)(a)(ii) caps funeral and burial expenses at the policy amount, which must be at least $1,750 and no more than $5,000.

q: Dan is injured in a Michigan auto accident on November 15, 2026. He earned $10,000 a month and cannot work for several months. He does not prove a lower income tax advantage. Ignoring other offsets, what is the most PIP pays for work loss for one 30-day period?
explain: Work loss is reduced 15% for tax advantage (85% of $10,000 = $8,500). It is then capped at $7,455, the 30-day maximum for accidents from Oct. 1, 2026 to Sept. 30, 2027. $7,201 was the cap for accidents from Oct. 1, 2025 to Sept. 30, 2026.

q: Michigan's no-fault law limits PIP benefits for replacement services to:
choices: $20 per day, for up to 3 years after the accident
$20 per day, for life
$40 per day, for up to 3 years after the accident
$600 per month, for 1 year
explain: Section 3107(1)(c) pays up to $20 per day for ordinary and necessary services during the first 3 years after the accident.

q: Under Michigan's no-fault law, PIP survivor's loss benefits are payable:
choices: To any relative, with no 30-day maximum, for the rest of the relative's life
To the deceased's estate, as a one-time $5,000 lump-sum payment
To dependents, with a 30-day maximum, for up to 3 years after the accident
To dependents, but only if the deceased was not at fault in the accident
explain: Section 3108 pays dependents for lost support and replacement services (up to $20/day). It is capped per 30 days ($7,455 for accidents Oct. 1, 2026 to Sept. 30, 2027) and is not payable beyond 3 years after the accident.

q: For Michigan auto policies issued or renewed after July 1, 2020, a named insured may choose all of the following PIP medical (allowable expense) limits EXCEPT:
choices: Unlimited coverage
explain: Section 3107c(1) lists $50,000 (Medicaid only), $250,000, $500,000 and no limit. An opt-out under 3107d is available to qualified persons. There is no $100,000 level.

q: Which applicant may choose the $50,000 PIP medical limit under Michigan's no-fault law?
choices: A Medicaid enrollee whose spouse and resident relatives have qualified health coverage, Medicaid, or other auto PIP
A Medicare Parts A and B enrollee whose spouse and resident relatives have qualified health coverage or other auto PIP
Any applicant age 60 or older
Any applicant who signs the DIFS-approved selection form
explain: Section 3107c(1)(a) limits the $50,000 level to a named insured enrolled in Medicaid, provided the household members also have QHC, Medicaid or other auto PIP medical coverage.

q: To opt out of PIP medical coverage entirely under Michigan's no-fault law, the named insured must:
choices: Be enrolled in Medicaid, with the spouse and resident relatives having qualified health coverage or other auto PIP
Have any employer health plan with an individual deductible of no more than $6,579
Carry a $250,000 PIP limit on another vehicle
Be enrolled in Medicare Parts A and B, with the spouse and resident relatives having qualified health coverage or other auto PIP
explain: Under 3107d(1) and (7)(c), only a 'qualified person' (Medicare Parts A and B) may opt out, and the household must have QHC or other auto PIP. Employer coverage that qualifies as QHC supports the $250,000-with-exclusions option (3109a(2)), not the opt-out.

q: A named insured renews a Michigan auto policy but never makes an effective PIP selection, and no premium payment creates a presumption of a different level. Under Michigan's no-fault law, which PIP medical level applies?
choices: Unlimited
explain: Under 3107c(4), unlimited coverage (3107c(1)(d)) applies when there is no effective selection and no premium-payment presumption under 3107c(3).

q: For the period July 1, 2026, to June 30, 2027, qualified health coverage under Michigan's no-fault law includes health coverage that does not exclude auto-accident injuries and has an annual individual deductible of no more than:
explain: The statutory base is $6,000, adjusted by medical CPI only when the change reaches $500. DIFS Bulletin 2026-08-INS keeps the cap at $6,579 for July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027.

q: Sue chose $250,000 PIP with an exclusion for household members who have qualified health coverage. Her husband, excluded because of his employer's qualified health coverage, loses that coverage. Under Michigan's no-fault law, within what time must she get PIP medical coverage for him?
choices: 10 days after the qualified health coverage ends
30 days after the qualified health coverage ends
60 days after the qualified health coverage ends
By the next policy renewal date
explain: Under 3109a(2)(d), the named insured must obtain the excluded coverage within 30 days after QHC terminates. Someone injured during that 30-day window may claim through the assigned claims plan.

q: Ann is injured in an auto accident. PIP medical benefits are payable under two policies, one with a $250,000 limit and one with a $500,000 limit. Under Michigan's no-fault law, what is the most PIP medical she can collect in total?
choices: Unlimited
explain: Under 3107c(6), when two or more policies apply, PIP medical is payable only up to the highest single available limit. The limits do not stack.

q: Under Michigan's no-fault law, an auto insurer that offers a managed care option for PIP allowable expenses must:
choices: Make the managed care option apply to all care, including emergency care
Price the managed care option the same as PIP without managed care
Also offer PIP allowable expense coverage not subject to managed care
Prohibit deductibles and co-pays for care provided under the option
explain: An insurer that offers a managed care option must also offer PIP allowable expense coverage that is not subject to it. The option must be offered uniformly where available, must carry a discount reflecting anticipated savings, may not apply to emergency care, and may include deductibles and co-pays. These rules are in Chapter 31A of the Insurance Code, added by the 2019 no-fault reform.

q: Tom is hurt as a passenger in his friend's insured car. Tom has no auto policy of his own, but he lives with his mother, who has a Michigan no-fault policy. Under Michigan's no-fault law, who pays Tom's PIP first?
choices: The insurer of the car's driver
The Michigan Assigned Claims Plan
The insurer of his friend, the car's owner
His mother's insurer
explain: Under 3114(1), a PIP policy covers the named insured, spouse and relatives of either domiciled in the same household. Tom is a resident relative, so his mother's insurer pays first.

q: An employee is hurt while driving a truck owned by her employer. She also has her own personal auto policy. Under Michigan's no-fault law, who pays her PIP?
choices: The insurer of the employer-furnished vehicle
Her own personal auto insurer
Her employer's workers' compensation insurer
The Michigan Assigned Claims Plan
explain: Section 3114(3) gives priority to the insurer of the furnished vehicle when an employee, spouse or resident relative is hurt while occupying an employer-owned or employer-registered vehicle. Workers' comp benefits are subtracted from PIP (3109(1)); they do not replace it.

q: A Michigan resident who has no auto insurance and lives alone is struck by an insured car in Michigan while walking. Under Michigan's no-fault law as amended in 2019, the pedestrian:
choices: Claims PIP from the insurer of the car's driver
Is not entitled to PIP benefits
Claims PIP from the insurer of the car's owner
Claims PIP through the Michigan Assigned Claims Plan
explain: As amended by 2019 PA 21, 3115 sends a non-occupant who has no own or household PIP policy to the assigned claims plan. Before the reform, such a pedestrian claimed from the insurers of the vehicle's owner or operator. (A nonresident who owns no Michigan-registered and insured vehicle is not entitled to PIP at all under 3113(c).)

q: A motorcyclist is hurt when another driver's car turns into his path. He has an auto policy on his own car, and the other car's owner is insured. Under Michigan's no-fault law, who is first in priority to pay the motorcyclist's PIP?
choices: The insurer that covers the motorcyclist's own car
The insurer of the motorcycle
The insurer of the other car's owner or registrant
The Michigan Assigned Claims Plan
explain: Under 3114(5), the order is: (a) the insurer of the motor vehicle's owner or registrant, (b) the insurer of the motor vehicle's operator, (c) the motorcycle operator's motor vehicle insurer, and (d) the motorcycle owner's motor vehicle insurer.

q: Michigan's no-fault law caps property protection insurance (PPI) benefits under one policy for all tangible property damaged in one accident at:
explain: Section 3121(5) caps PPI at $1,000,000 per policy for all property damage from one accident. It pays the lesser of repair cost or replacement cost less depreciation, plus loss of use.

q: A driver loses control on a Michigan road and damages three things owned by strangers: a fence, a properly parked car, and a car moving in the next lane. Under Michigan's no-fault law, which items does the driver's PPI pay for?
choices: The moving car and the parked car only
The fence and the parked car only
The fence, the parked car, and the moving car
The fence only
explain: Section 3123(1)(a) excludes vehicles and their contents unless parked so as not to cause unreasonable risk. A moving car is excluded. Its owner looks to collision coverage or the mini-tort.

q: A driver with a Michigan no-fault policy causes each of the following losses to property owned by others. Under Michigan's no-fault law, which loss is NOT payable by the driver's property protection insurance (PPI)?
choices: Damage to a storefront in Detroit
Damage to a properly parked car in Lansing
Loss of use of a damaged business property in Michigan
Damage to a building in Toledo, Ohio
explain: Section 3123(2) bars PPI for accidents occurring outside Michigan. Residual PD liability (at least $10,000) covers out-of-state property damage instead.

q: Under Michigan's no-fault law, an injured person may sue a negligent insured driver for noneconomic loss only if the injured person suffered:
choices: Death, serious impairment of body function, or permanent serious disfigurement
Medical expenses over $3,000 or more than 30 days of lost work
An injury lasting at least 1 year
An injury that required medical treatment, hospitalization, or time off work
explain: Section 3135(1) sets this tort threshold. 'Serious impairment' has no minimum duration under 3135(5).

q: In an auto tort suit for noneconomic damages, Michigan's no-fault law allows no damages to be awarded to a party who is:
choices: Partly at fault
At least 25% at fault
More than 50% at fault
Insured for unlimited PIP
explain: Section 3135(2)(b) applies comparative fault but bars recovery by a party more than 50% at fault.

q: For a Michigan accident after July 1, 2020, the no-fault mini-tort lets a vehicle owner recover vehicle damage not covered by insurance from an at-fault driver up to:
explain: Section 3135(3)(e) raised the mini-tort from $1,000 to $3,000 for accidents after July 1, 2020. A claimant more than 50% at fault cannot recover, and the case is brought in small claims when possible.

q: Kim chose a $250,000 PIP medical limit. After an accident caused by a negligent insured driver, she has $400,000 in medical expenses. Under Michigan's no-fault law, the medical expenses above her PIP limit:
choices: May be recovered by suing the at-fault driver
Cannot be recovered
May be recovered from the Michigan Assigned Claims Plan
May be recovered from the Michigan Catastrophic Claims Association
explain: Section 3135(3)(c) keeps tort liability for allowable expenses, work loss and survivor's loss above any 3107c limit (or the daily, monthly and 3-year limits). This is one reason higher BI liability limits matter.

q: For policies issued or renewed from July 1, 2025, to June 30, 2027, the Michigan Catastrophic Claims Association (MCCA) retention per loss occurrence is:
explain: The MCCA reports a $675,000 retention for July 1, 2025 to June 30, 2027. The $580,000 statutory base (2019 to 2021) is adjusted every 2 years by the lesser of 6% or CPI. $250,000 was the original 1978 retention.

q: Michigan's no-fault law requires a person claiming PIP through the Michigan Assigned Claims Plan to notify the Michigan Automobile Insurance Placement Facility within:
choices: 30 days after the accident
60 days after the first medical bill
1 year after the accident
3 years after the accident
explain: Section 3174 requires notice to the MAIPF within 1 year after the accident. The MAIPF then assigns the claim to an insurer.

q: Under Michigan's no-fault law, what is the maximum PIP medical (allowable expense) benefit generally payable through the Michigan Assigned Claims Plan?
choices: There is no maximum
explain: Section 3172(7) caps MACP allowable expenses at the 3107c(1)(b) limit of $250,000. The cap is $2,000,000 for persons injured during the 30-day gap after losing qualified health coverage.

q: If no written notice of injury was given and no PIP benefits were paid, Michigan's no-fault law requires an action to recover PIP benefits to be started no later than:
choices: 6 months after the accident
1 year after the accident
2 years after the accident
3 years after the accident
explain: Under 3145(1), the 1-year deadline runs from the accident. If notice was given or benefits were paid, suit may be filed within 1 year after the most recent loss is incurred, but recovery reaches back only 1 year (3145(2)).

q: Under Michigan's auto cancellation law, after an auto liability policy has been in effect for 55 days, the insurer may cancel it for a reason other than nonpayment only if the named insured or a household or customary operator:
choices: Is judged by the insurer to be an unacceptable risk after a driving record review
Has two at-fault accidents in the policy period
Moves to another Michigan county
Has a license suspended or revoked in the policy period, and it has become final
explain: After 55 days (or immediately on a renewal), 3220 allows cancellation only for a final license suspension or revocation. 'Risk unacceptable' is a ground only during the first 55 days.

q: Under Michigan's auto cancellation law, a cancellation notice must be mailed at least how many days before the effective date, and must state that the insured may appeal to DIFS within how many days from the date of mailing?
choices: Mailed 10 days before; appeal within 30 days
Mailed 20 days before; appeal within 7 days
Mailed 30 days before; appeal within 10 days
Mailed 45 days before; appeal within 20 days
explain: Section 3224 requires certified mail, return receipt requested (delivery is equivalent), at least 20 days ahead, with reasons and a bold notice of the 7-day appeal right. A cancellation during the first 55 days is not appealable.

q: Michigan's auto cancellation law does not treat an insurer's refusal to renew an auto liability policy as a cancellation if the insurer mails notice by first-class mail at least how many days before the termination date?
choices: 10 days
20 days
45 days
60 days
explain: Section 3204(2) sets this 20-day rule. The Essential Insurance Act (MCL 500.2123) separately requires 30 days' notice with specific reasons for a 'termination'.

q: Under Michigan's Aftermarket Crash Parts Act, if an insurer asks for non-OEM aftermarket crash parts to be used, the repair facility may use them only if:
choices: The insured gets a written estimate listing each non-OEM part, with a notice in at least 10-point bold type
DIFS approves each part in advance
The vehicle is more than 5 years old or has been driven more than 100,000 miles
The insured signs a written consent form and pays the difference between the OEM and the non-OEM part prices
explain: Section 257.1363 requires the written estimate and a bold disclosure that the parts come from a source other than the manufacturer, with warranties provided by their manufacturer, distributor or insurer.

q: A rental company that was not itself negligent rents a car for 30 days or less. The authorized driver negligently injures someone while using the car. Under the Michigan Vehicle Code, what is the most the company can be held liable for as owner?
choices: Nothing
$20,000 per person and $40,000 per accident
$50,000 per person and $100,000 per accident
$250,000 per person and $500,000 per accident
explain: The short-term lessor is liable only when an authorized driver or an immediate family member is driving, and its liability is capped at 20/40 unless it was negligent. It must notify the lessee of the cap (257.401(4)).

q: Lisa has her own Michigan no-fault policy. She is hurt while driving a car she rented for a 1-week vacation in Michigan. Under Michigan's no-fault law, who pays her PIP first?
choices: No one
The Michigan Assigned Claims Plan
The rental company's insurer
Her own auto insurer
explain: PIP is owed without regard to fault (3105(2)), and 3114(1) applies the injured person's own (or household) policy first. A 1-week renter is not an 'owner' (more than 30 days is required).

sub: Personal Auto: Damage to Your Auto
q: The limited collision coverage that Michigan law requires an insurer to offer a new applicant for a private passenger auto:
choices: Pays with no deductible, but only if the driver was not more than 50% at fault
Pays regardless of fault, with no deductible
Pays regardless of fault, with the deductible waived only if the other driver is uninsured
Pays only for collisions with animals
explain: Section 3037(1)(a) requires the offered limited collision to pay without a deductible, but only when the operator was not substantially (more than 50%) at fault (3037(8)(b)). Broad form collision pays regardless of fault, with the deductible waived when the operator was not substantially at fault. Insurers may also sell standard and limited collision with deductibles (3037(2)).

q: Under Michigan law, uninsured/underinsured motorists coverage:
choices: Is optional coverage the insured may choose to buy
Is part of the PIP coverage
Is required unless the insured rejects it in writing
Must be bought with limits equal to the bodily injury liability limits
explain: DIFS lists UM and UIM among optional coverages, and the Michigan Supreme Court (Rory v Continental, 2005) called UM coverage optional, not required by the no-fault act, with its terms governed by contract.
source: DIFS auto insurance FAQ; Rory v Continental Ins Co, 473 Mich 457 (2005)

q: If you buy an additional private passenger auto during the policy period, liability coverage under the 2018 ISO Personal Auto Policy applies to it only if you ask the insurer to insure it within:
choices: 4 days after you become the owner
14 days after you become the owner
30 days after you become the owner
60 days after you become the owner
explain: Under Definition K.2.a of the 2018 PAP, a newly acquired auto gets the broadest coverage on any declared vehicle (for coverages other than Part D) if you ask within 14 days. If you ask later, coverage begins when you ask.

q: You buy a second car. No auto in your Declarations has collision coverage. Under the 2018 ISO Personal Auto Policy, within how many days must you ask for collision coverage on the new car, and what deductible applies to a loss before you ask?
choices: Within 4 days; $250 deductible
Within 4 days; $500 deductible
Within 14 days; $500 deductible
Within 30 days; $1,000 deductible
explain: Definition K.2.b(2) of the 2018 PAP: if no declared auto has collision, you must ask within 4 days, and a $500 collision deductible applies to a loss that occurs before you ask. If any declared auto has collision, the window is 14 days.

q: Under the 2018 ISO Personal Auto Policy, Part A supplementary payments include up to how much for bail bonds and up to how much a day for loss of earnings to attend hearings or trials at the insurer's request?
choices: Bail bonds $250; loss of earnings $200 a day
Bail bonds $250; loss of earnings $250 a day
Bail bonds $1,000; loss of earnings $100 a day
Bail bonds $2,000; loss of earnings $250 a day
explain: The 2018 PAP pays bail bonds up to $250 and loss of earnings up to $250 a day, in addition to the limit. The $2,000 bail bond amount is from the Business Auto form.
source: ISO PP 00 01 09 18, Part A Supplementary Payments; ISO CA 00 01 11 20 Sec. II.A.2

q: The 2018 ISO Personal Auto Policy's liability exclusion for a vehicle used as a public or livery conveyance includes:
choices: Driving for a volunteer or charitable purpose, such as delivering meals to seniors
A share-the-expense car pool in which riders split fuel and parking costs
Commuting to and from work
Time logged into a transportation network platform as a driver
explain: Exclusion A.5 of the 2018 PAP expressly includes time logged into a TNC platform as a driver. It does not apply to share-the-expense car pools or volunteer or charitable use.
source: ISO PP 00 01 09 18, Part A Exclusion A.5

q: Under Part C – Uninsured Motorists Coverage of the Personal Auto Policy, an 'uninsured motor vehicle' includes all of the following EXCEPT:
choices: A hit-and-run vehicle whose owner or operator cannot be identified and which hits you
A vehicle owned by a governmental unit or agency
A vehicle whose insurer denies coverage or becomes insolvent
A vehicle with bodily injury limits below the financial responsibility minimum of the state where your covered auto is principally garaged
explain: Part C excludes vehicles owned by a governmental unit or agency from the definition. It also excludes vehicles owned by or furnished or available for the regular use of you or a family member, self-insured vehicles (unless the self-insurer is insolvent), and others.
source: ISO PP 00 01 09 18, Part C Definition C

sub: Personal Auto: Damage to Your Auto
q: Which one of the following losses is treated as Other Than Collision under Part D – Coverage for Damage to Your Auto of the Personal Auto Policy?
choices: Hitting a guardrail
Backing into a parked car
Hitting a deer
Rolling the car over
explain: Contact with a bird or animal is listed as Other Than Collision. Upset (rollover) and impact with another vehicle or object are collision.
source: ISO PP 00 01 09 18, Part D Insuring Agreement B

sub: Personal Auto: Damage to Your Auto
q: After a covered total theft of your covered auto, the 2018 ISO Personal Auto Policy pays temporary transportation expenses of:
choices: Up to $20 per day, maximum $600, starting immediately
Up to $30 per day, maximum $900, starting 24 hours after the theft
Up to $30 per day, maximum $900, starting 48 hours after the theft
Up to $50 per day, with no maximum
explain: The 2018 PAP pays without a deductible up to $30/day and a $900 maximum. For total theft, payment starts 48 hours after the theft; for other losses it starts once the auto is out of use for more than 24 hours. Older editions used $20/$600.
source: ISO PP 00 01 09 18, Part D Transportation Expenses

q: According to DIFS, a named non-owner or extended non-owned coverage endorsement on a Michigan no-fault policy provides:
choices: Physical damage coverage only, for vehicles furnished for the named person's regular use
PIP, PPI, and residual liability for the named person, spouse, and all resident relatives
Residual liability only, for the named person and spouse
PIP coverage only
explain: Bulletin 96-02 says these endorsements provide only residual liability, only for the named person and spouse, and exclude other resident relatives. Insurers should make clear that they do not meet no-fault requirements.

q: The Extended Non-Owned Coverage endorsement to the Personal Auto Policy is designed for someone who:
choices: Owns a second car that is insured under a separate personal auto policy
Regularly drives a vehicle furnished by an employer
Owns a motorcycle
Owns a motor home rented to others
explain: The endorsement removes the PAP exclusion for vehicles furnished or available for the named individual's regular use, for liability and, if bought, med pay. It does not cover vehicles owned by the individual or family members.
source: ISO PP 03 06 01 05; ISO PP 00 01 09 18 Part A Exclusion B.2

q: Which one of the following vehicles would typically be covered under the Personal Auto Policy by adding the Miscellaneous Type Vehicle endorsement?
choices: A motor home
A snowmobile
A semi-tractor used for hauling freight
A private passenger sedan
explain: The endorsement (PP 03 23) is used for motor homes, motorcycles and similar vehicles, ATVs, dune buggies and golf carts. Snowmobiles have a separate endorsement, and sedans are already covered autos.
source: ISO PP 03 23 (FC&S, Miscellaneous Type Vehicle Endorsement)

sub: Commercial Auto: Business Auto Coverage Form
q: When symbol 7 is shown for a coverage under the 2020 ISO Business Auto Coverage Form, a newly acquired auto gets that coverage only if the insurer already covers all owned autos for that coverage, or the auto replaces a previously owned auto that had it, and the insured asks within:
choices: 4 days after acquiring it
14 days after acquiring it
30 days after acquiring it
60 days after acquiring it
explain: Section I.B.2 of the 2020 form sets this 30-day rule for symbol 7. Symbols 1 through 6 and 19 automatically cover autos acquired during the policy period.

sub: Commercial Auto: Business Auto Coverage Form
q: A business wants liability coverage for its employees' personal cars when they are used to run company errands. Which covered auto symbol of the Business Auto Coverage Form applies?
choices: Symbol 2: Owned Autos Only
Symbol 8: Hired Autos Only
Symbol 9: Non-owned Autos Only
Symbol 19: Mobile Equipment Subject to Compulsory or Financial Responsibility Law
explain: Symbol 9 covers autos you do not own, lease, hire, rent or borrow that are used in your business, including employees' autos. Symbol 8 specifically excludes autos borrowed from employees.

sub: Commercial Auto: Business Auto Coverage Form
q: Under the 2020 ISO Business Auto Coverage Form, supplementary payments include the cost of bail bonds up to:
explain: Section II.A.2.a(2) of the 2020 BACF pays up to $2,000 for bail bonds, plus loss of earnings up to $250 a day. The PAP bail bond limit is $250.

q: A repair shop's garagekeepers coverage pays for hail damage to a customer's car while it is in the shop's care, regardless of the shop's liability and before the customer's own insurance. On what basis is the coverage written?
choices: Direct primary
Garage liability
Legal liability
Direct excess
explain: Legal liability pays only if the shop is legally liable. Direct excess pays regardless of liability but only in excess of other collectible insurance. Direct primary pays regardless of liability, as primary.

q: The Truckers Coverage Form is designed for:
choices: Families insuring private passenger autos for personal use
Franchised auto dealers
Businesses that transport property by auto for hire
Repair garages and service stations
explain: The Truckers form provides liability and physical damage (including trailer interchange) for those transporting property for hire. Dealers use the Auto Dealers or Garage form.

q: An executive has a company-furnished car and no personal auto policy. Which commercial auto endorsement covers the executive while driving non-owned autos?
choices: Additional Insured: Lessor
Drive Other Car Coverage
Garagekeepers Coverage
Mobile Equipment
explain: The DOC endorsement (CA 99 10) gives a named individual (and resident spouse) PAP-like non-owned auto coverage under the commercial policy.

sub: Commercial Auto: Motor Carrier Act of 1980
q: Under federal motor carrier rules (Motor Carrier Act of 1980), a for-hire interstate carrier hauling nonhazardous property in vehicles with a gross vehicle weight rating of 10,001 pounds or more must carry minimum public liability of:
explain: Under 387.9, the minimum is $750,000 for nonhazardous property. Oil and most hazardous materials require $1,000,000, and certain bulk hazardous substances, explosives and radioactive materials require $5,000,000.

sub: PAP Liability > Bodily Injury and Property Damage (insuring agreement, who is insured)
q: Kim's son lives with her. He causes an accident while driving a friend's car with permission, and no one in Kim's household owns that car or has it for regular use. Under Part A – Liability Coverage of Kim's 2018 ISO Personal Auto Policy, her son is:
choices: An insured
Not an insured
An insured only if the friend has no auto insurance
An insured only if the friend's insurer denies the claim
explain: Part A insureds include you or any family member for the ownership, maintenance or use of any auto or trailer. Coverage for a vehicle you do not own is excess over any other collectible insurance, so it applies whether or not the friend is insured.
source: ISO PP 00 01 09 18 (Personal Auto Policy), Part A – Liability Coverage, Insuring Agreement B.1, Exclusions B.2–B.3 and Other Insurance; Definitions F ('family member')

sub: PAP Liability > Bodily Injury and Property Damage (insuring agreement, who is insured)
q: Under Part A – Liability Coverage of the 2018 ISO Personal Auto Policy, the defense costs the insurer incurs are:
choices: Included within the limit of liability
Shared equally by the insurer and the insured
Paid only if the insured is found liable
Paid in addition to the limit of liability
explain: The Part A insuring agreement states that, in addition to the limit of liability, the insurer pays all defense costs it incurs. Its duty to settle or defend ends when the limit is exhausted by payment of judgments or settlements.
source: ISO PP 00 01 09 18, Part A – Liability Coverage, Insuring Agreement A

sub: Personal Auto > Medical Payments Coverage (Part B)
q: Under Part B – Medical Payments Coverage of the 2018 ISO Personal Auto Policy, the insurer pays only for expenses for services rendered within what period from the date of the accident?
choices: 1 year
2 years
3 years
5 years
explain: Part B pays reasonable expenses for necessary medical and funeral services because of bodily injury caused by an accident, but only for services rendered within three years from the date of the accident.
source: ISO PP 00 01 09 18, Part B – Medical Payments Coverage, Insuring Agreement A

sub: Personal Auto > Medical Payments Coverage (Part B)
q: Under Part B – Medical Payments Coverage of the 2018 ISO Personal Auto Policy, insureds include all of the following EXCEPT:
choices: The named insured, struck by a car while walking
A neighbor, struck by the named insured's car while walking
A family member, while occupying a friend's car
A guest, while occupying the named insured's covered auto
explain: Part B insureds are you or any family member while occupying, or as a pedestrian when struck by, a motor vehicle designed for use mainly on public roads (or a trailer), and any other person while occupying your covered auto. Someone else struck as a pedestrian is not a Part B insured.
source: ISO PP 00 01 09 18, Part B – Medical Payments Coverage, Insuring Agreement B

sub: Personal Auto > Duties After an Accident or Loss (Part E)
q: Under Part E – Duties After An Accident Or Loss of the 2018 ISO Personal Auto Policy, the insurer has no duty to provide coverage when a person fails to comply with a listed duty if:
choices: The failure is prejudicial to the insurer
The person seeking coverage caused the accident
The claim is for bodily injury only
The person has made an earlier claim under the policy
explain: Part E opens: 'We have no duty to provide coverage under this Policy if the failure to comply with the following duties is prejudicial to us.'
source: ISO PP 00 01 09 18, Part E – Duties After An Accident Or Loss (opening paragraph)

sub: Personal Auto > Duties After an Accident or Loss (Part E)
q: Under Part E of the 2018 ISO Personal Auto Policy, a person seeking Uninsured Motorists Coverage must also:
choices: Obtain the insurer's consent before seeking medical treatment
File suit against the uninsured driver before making a claim
Promptly notify the police if a hit-and-run driver is involved
Permit the insurer to inspect the other driver's car
explain: Besides the general duties (prompt notice, cooperation, sending legal papers, exams, records and proof of loss), a person seeking Uninsured Motorists Coverage must promptly notify the police if a hit-and-run driver is involved and promptly send copies of legal papers if a suit is brought.
source: ISO PP 00 01 09 18, Part E – Duties After An Accident Or Loss, A–C

q: Under Michigan's no-fault law, a deductible on the PIP coverage of a Michigan Personal Auto Policy applies only to benefits payable to:
choices: Any person occupying the named insured's covered auto
Any pedestrian struck by the named insured's covered auto
Any passenger who has no auto insurance of their own
The named insured, spouse and resident relatives
explain: An insurer may offer a PIP deductible at an appropriately reduced premium, but the deductible applies only to benefits payable to the person named in the policy, the spouse, and any relative of either domiciled in the same household. It does not apply to other occupants, pedestrians or passengers.
source: MCL 500.3109(3) (legislature.mi.gov, read Oct. 2026). ISO's Michigan PIP endorsement for the Personal Auto Policy is Personal Injury Protection Coverage – Michigan, current edition PP 05 90 03 26 per Wolters Kluwer 'Personal Automobile Policy Forms and Endorsements' list (generated Oct. 13, 2026)

q: Under Michigan's no-fault law, which person may waive the work loss part of PIP coverage in exchange for a reduced premium?
choices: A person enrolled in Medicaid whose relatives have health coverage
A person 60 or older not eligible for work loss benefits
Any named insured who signs a rejection form at policy inception
A 55-year-old who has retired from work
explain: Only a person 60 years of age or older who would not be eligible for work loss benefits may waive work loss coverage, by signing a waiver on a form provided by the insurer. The insurer must offer a reduced premium, and the waiver applies only to the persons who sign it. A 55-year-old does not meet the age requirement. Medicaid enrollment is a condition for choosing the $50,000 PIP medical limit, not for waiving work loss.

sub: PAP Endorsements > Property Protection Coverage - Michigan (3121)
q: Pat, the named insured on a Michigan auto policy, backs Pat's insured car into Pat's own garage in Michigan. Under Michigan's no-fault law, Pat's property protection insurance (PPI) pays for the garage damage:
choices: Nothing
Up to $3,000
explain: PPI excludes property owned by the person named in the policy, the spouse, or a resident relative of either if that person was the owner, registrant or operator of a vehicle involved in the accident.

sub: PAP Endorsements > Property Protection Coverage - Michigan (3121)
q: While servicing a customer's car, a mechanic accidentally drives it into a tool cabinet inside the repair shop. Under Michigan's no-fault law, property protection insurance (PPI) benefits for the tool cabinet are:
choices: Payable without regard to fault
Payable only if the mechanic was not at fault
Not payable
Payable only after the shop's property insurance pays
explain: Accidental damage to tangible property under PPI does not include damage to property, other than the insured motor vehicle, that occurs within the course of a business of repairing, servicing or otherwise maintaining motor vehicles.

q: The 2010 ISO Garage Coverage Form was designed to give a garage business, in one coverage form:
choices: Physical damage coverage only, with liability written on a separate policy
Auto liability only, with premises liability written on a separate policy
Liability for garage operations and autos, plus garagekeepers and physical damage
Liability and trailer interchange coverage for for-hire truckers
explain: The form's sections are Liability (for 'garage operations' other than covered autos and for covered autos), Garagekeepers, Physical Damage, Garage Conditions and Definitions, so it combined the general liability and auto exposures of a garage. ISO eliminated the Garage form with its 2013 commercial auto revision.
source: ISO CA 00 05 03 10 (Garage Coverage Form), Sections II–VI and VI.H ('garage operations'); Rough Notes PF&M, 'CA 00 05 Garage Coverage Form Analysis' (03/10 ed.); Rough Notes PF&M, 'ISO Motor Carrier Coverage Form Available Endorsements And Their Uses' (Oct. 2022): 'CA 00 05 Garage Coverage Form and CA 00 10 Business Auto Physical Damage Coverage Form were eliminated with the 10 13 edition'

q: Under ISO's 2010 commercial auto program, which business is eligible for the Garage Coverage Form?
choices: A franchised auto dealer
A for-hire trucking company
A furniture store with delivery trucks
A plumbing contractor with service vans
explain: The garage form was issued to franchised and nonfranchised auto dealers, whose general liability and auto exposures overlap, so one form covered both. A for-hire trucker was written on the Truckers or Motor Carrier form, and a furniture store or plumbing contractor is not a garage business. A 2003 North Carolina Reinsurance Facility circular reports that ISO removed auto service operations, such as repair shops and service stations, from garage program eligibility, so a dealer is used here.
source: FC&S, 'Standard Commercial Auto Program' (PropertyCasualty360, Mar. 18, 2010), eligibility; Rough Notes PF&M, 'ISO Garage Coverage Form Archive' (Oct. 2022), CA 00 05 Garage Coverage Form Analysis (03/10 edition), Introduction; North Carolina Reinsurance Facility Circular RF-03-1 (Jan. 10, 2003), 'Removal of Eligibility of Auto Service Classifications from the Garage Policy Program'

sub: Commercial Auto Forms > Business Automobile Physical Damage
q: The 2010 ISO Business Auto Physical Damage Coverage Form provides:
choices: Physical damage coverage only, with no liability coverage
Liability coverage only, for hired and non-owned autos
Liability and physical damage coverage for auto dealers
Physical damage coverage for customers' autos left for service
explain: The form has four sections (Covered Autos, Physical Damage Coverage, Business Auto Conditions, Definitions) and no liability section; it offers Comprehensive, Specified Causes of Loss and Collision on owned or hired autos (symbols 1–5). ISO eliminated it with the 2013 revision.
source: ISO CA 00 10 03 10 (Business Auto Physical Damage Coverage Form), Sections I–IV; Rough Notes PF&M, 'ISO Motor Carrier Coverage Form Available Endorsements And Their Uses' (Oct. 2022): 'CA 00 05 Garage Coverage Form and CA 00 10 Business Auto Physical Damage Coverage Form were eliminated with the 10 13 edition'

sub: Commercial Auto Forms > Motor Carrier (coverage form)
q: Which ISO commercial auto coverage form is designed for both for-hire carriers and private carriers that haul their own goods?
choices: Business Auto Physical Damage Coverage Form
Garage Coverage Form
Truckers Coverage Form
Motor Carrier Coverage Form
explain: The Motor Carrier form defines a 'motor carrier' as a person or organization providing transportation by auto in the furtherance of a commercial enterprise, and FC&S says it was built for common and private motor carriers. The Truckers form defines a 'trucker' as one in the business of transporting property by auto for hire.
source: ISO CA 00 20 03 10 (Motor Carrier Coverage Form), Section VI.L; ISO CA 00 12 10 01 (Truckers Coverage Form), Section VI.Q; FC&S, 'Motor Carrier Coverage Form' (PropertyCasualty360, June 25, 2008)

sub: Commercial Auto Forms > Motor Carrier (coverage form)
q: A motor carrier has another carrier's trailer in its possession under a written trailer interchange agreement in which it assumes liability for loss to the trailer. Under the 2010 ISO Motor Carrier Coverage Form, damage to that trailer is covered by:
choices: Liability Coverage
Trailer Interchange Coverage
Garagekeepers Coverage
Auto Medical Payments Coverage
explain: Trailer Interchange Coverage (Section III) pays all sums the insured legally must pay as damages because of loss to a trailer it does not own, under Comprehensive, Specified Causes of Loss or Collision; symbol 69 describes such trailers. Liability Coverage excludes property in the insured's care, custody or control.
source: ISO CA 00 20 03 10, Section I.A (symbol 69), Section III.A.1, Section II.B.6 (Care, Custody Or Control)

sub: Coverage Form Sections > Physical Damage Coverage
q: A business carries only Specified Causes of Loss Coverage on its van under the 2020 ISO Business Auto Coverage Form. Which loss is covered?
choices: The van hits a deer
A rock thrown up by a passing truck cracks the windshield
The van slides into a guardrail
The van is damaged by a flood while parked
explain: Specified Causes of Loss covers only fire, lightning or explosion; theft; windstorm, hail or earthquake; flood; mischief or vandalism; and the sinking, burning, collision or derailment of a conveyance carrying the auto. Hitting an animal and glass breakage are paid under Comprehensive, and hitting an object is Collision.
source: ISO CA 00 01 11 20 (Business Auto Coverage Form), Section III.A.1 and A.3

sub: Coverage Form Sections > Physical Damage Coverage
q: Under the 2020 ISO Business Auto Coverage Form, the Transportation Expenses coverage extension pays after the total theft of a covered auto only if the stolen auto is:
choices: A private passenger auto with Comprehensive or Specified Causes of Loss
Any type of auto, if Collision Coverage is carried on that auto
Any type of auto, if any physical damage coverage is carried on it
An auto hired without a driver under a written rental contract
explain: The extension pays up to $30 a day, to a maximum of $900, for temporary transportation after the total theft of a covered auto of the private passenger type, only if Comprehensive or Specified Causes of Loss Coverage is carried on it, starting 48 hours after the theft. The 2013 edition paid $20 a day, to $600.
source: ISO CA 00 01 11 20, Section III.A.4.a; ISO CA 00 01 10 13, Section III.A.4.a compared

q: A delivery van insured under the 2020 ISO Business Auto Coverage Form overturns. Which loss is excluded under Covered Autos Liability Coverage?
choices: Injury to a pedestrian struck by the overturning van
Damage to customers' packages being carried in the van
Damage to another driver's car hit by the van
Damage to a storefront struck by the sliding van
explain: The Care, Custody Or Control exclusion removes property damage to property owned or transported by the insured or in the insured's care, custody or control, except liability assumed under a sidetrack agreement.
source: ISO CA 00 01 11 20, Section II.B.6 (Care, Custody Or Control)

q: Under Covered Autos Liability Coverage of the 2020 ISO Business Auto Coverage Form, which injury is excluded?
choices: A motorist hurt when the truck runs a red light
A pedestrian hit as the truck backs up to a loading dock
A bystander hurt by a forklift, not attached to the truck, unloading it
A bystander hurt by a power lift gate attached to the truck during unloading
explain: The form excludes bodily injury or property damage resulting from the movement of property by a mechanical device (other than a hand truck) unless the device is attached to the covered auto.
source: ISO CA 00 01 11 20, Section II.B.8 (Movement Of Property By Mechanical Device)

q: Under the 2020 ISO Business Auto Coverage Form, which loss to a covered auto is paid under Comprehensive Coverage?
choices: Engine damage from mechanical breakdown
A tire blowout caused by a pothole
Loss in resale value after a covered loss is repaired
A windshield broken by a falling tree branch
explain: Physical Damage Coverage excludes loss due and confined to wear and tear, freezing, mechanical or electrical breakdown, or blowouts, punctures or other road damage to tires (unless from total theft), and loss due to diminution in value. Glass breakage and falling objects are paid under Comprehensive.
source: ISO CA 00 01 11 20, Section III.A.3, B.3 and B.6; Section V.E ('diminution in value')

q: Under the Other Insurance condition of the 2020 ISO Business Auto Coverage Form, when no insured contract is involved, Covered Autos Liability Coverage for a covered auto (not a trailer) that the named insured does not own is:
choices: Excess over any other collectible insurance
Primary insurance
Shared equally with any other insurance
Void if any other insurance applies
explain: The form is primary for covered autos you own and excess over any other collectible insurance for covered autos you don't own. Separate rules apply to trailers, to Hired Auto Physical Damage (hired autos are deemed owned) and to liability assumed under an insured contract (primary).

q: A business has a Business Auto policy with a $1,000,000 limit and a second auto policy from the same insurer with a $500,000 limit that was not written as excess. Both apply to one accident. Under the 2020 ISO Business Auto Coverage Form, the most the insurer will pay is:
explain: Under the Two Or More Coverage Forms Or Policies Issued By Us condition, the aggregate maximum limit under all forms or policies issued by the insurer or an affiliate cannot exceed the highest applicable limit under any one of them. The condition does not apply to a policy issued specifically as excess over the Business Auto form.
source: ISO CA 00 01 11 20, Section IV.B.8 (Two Or More Coverage Forms Or Policies Issued By Us)

q: None of the following vehicles is subject to a compulsory or financial responsibility law. Under the 2020 ISO Business Auto Coverage Form, which one is an "auto" rather than "mobile equipment"?
choices: A bulldozer used only at construction job sites
A truck with permanently attached street-cleaning equipment
A forklift used only inside the insured's warehouse
A crawler-tread excavator moved between job sites by trailer
explain: Bulldozers, forklifts and vehicles on crawler treads are mobile equipment. Self-propelled vehicles with permanently attached equipment designed primarily for snow removal, road maintenance (not construction) or street cleaning are not mobile equipment but are considered autos.
source: ISO CA 00 01 11 20, Section V.B ('auto') and V.K ('mobile equipment')

q: Under the 2020 ISO Business Auto Coverage Form, which one of the following is an "insured contract"?
choices: A rental agreement's promise to pay for damage to the auto the insured rents
An agreement to rent an auto to the insured with a driver
A promise holding a for-hire trucker harmless for the insured's use of its authorized route
A lease of premises
explain: Insured contracts include a lease of premises, a sidetrack agreement, certain easements, municipal indemnity obligations, assumptions of another's tort liability, and auto rental agreements. They exclude the part of a rental agreement obligating you to pay for damage to the rented auto, rentals of autos with a driver, and agreements holding a for-hire trucker harmless for your use of its authorized route.

q: Under the 2020 ISO Lessor – Additional Insured And Loss Payee endorsement, a "leased auto" described in the Schedule is considered:
choices: A covered auto you hire
A non-owned auto
A covered auto you own
Mobile equipment
explain: The endorsement states that a scheduled leased auto will be considered a covered auto you own and not a covered auto you hire or borrow. It also adds the lessor as an insured and as a loss payee.
source: ISO CA 20 01 11 20 (Lessor – Additional Insured And Loss Payee), A.1

q: XYZ leases a truck from LeaseCo under a lease requiring XYZ to provide direct primary insurance for LeaseCo. XYZ's 2020 ISO Lessor – Additional Insured And Loss Payee endorsement schedules the truck and names LeaseCo as the lessor. An XYZ employee negligently injures a pedestrian while driving it. Under Covered Autos Liability Coverage, LeaseCo is:
choices: An insured
Not an insured
An insured only if it paid part of the premium
An insured only for damage to the truck itself
explain: The lessor named in the Schedule is an insured for bodily injury or property damage resulting from the acts or omissions of the named insured, its employees or agents, or any person (other than the lessor or its employees or agents) operating the leased auto with permission. The endorsement also says the lessor is not liable for the named insured's premiums.
source: ISO CA 20 01 11 20, A.2, D and E ('leased auto')

q: When a vehicle is described in the Mobile Equipment endorsement to the Business Auto Coverage Form, it is treated as:
choices: A covered auto, excluding liability from operating its attached machinery
A covered auto, including liability from operating its attached machinery
Mobile equipment, covered only while carried or towed by a covered auto
Mobile equipment, covered only for physical damage
explain: The endorsement treats the described vehicles as covered autos and not mobile equipment for the scheduled coverages. Liability coverage does not apply to bodily injury or property damage resulting from the operation of machinery or equipment on, attached to or part of those vehicles.
source: FC&S, 'Business Auto Endorsements' (PropertyCasualty360, Sept. 15, 2015) on ISO CA 20 15 10 13; Rough Notes PF&M, 'CA 20 15 Mobile Equipment' (Oct. 2022); current edition CA 20 15 11 20 per Wolters Kluwer 'Commercial Automobile Policy Forms and Endorsements' list (generated Oct. 13, 2026)

q: A contractor's crawler-mounted scissors lift is described in the Mobile Equipment endorsement to its Business Auto policy, with Covered Autos Liability Coverage scheduled for it. Which accident is covered under that coverage?
choices: The lift's platform malfunctions and falls on a subcontractor's worker during use
The lift arm strikes a power line while being raised
The lift vehicle strikes a car while crossing a highway between job sites
The lift's outriggers crush a parked car as they are extended
explain: A scheduled vehicle is covered while used as a vehicle, but liability does not apply to injury or damage resulting from operation of the machinery or equipment on or attached to it. Rough Notes gives this example: the policy responds when the lift vehicle hits an SUV while crossing a highway, but not when the lift portion malfunctions and falls on a worker.
source: Rough Notes PF&M, 'CA 20 15 Mobile Equipment' (Oct. 2022), Scenarios 1–2; FC&S (PropertyCasualty360, Sept. 15, 2015) on CA 20 15 10 13

sub: CA Endorsements > Michigan Personal Injury Protection (3107)
q: A Michigan company's Business Auto policy shows symbol 5 next to Personal Injury Protection. Under the 2020 ISO Business Auto Coverage Form, which autos have PIP?
choices: Every auto the company owns, hires or borrows, wherever it is garaged
Owned autos required by state law to have no-fault benefits
Only autos described in the Declarations for which a premium is shown
Only non-owned autos used in connection with the company's business
explain: Symbol 5 (Owned Autos Subject To No-fault) covers only autos the named insured owns that are required to have no-fault benefits in the state where they are licensed or principally garaged, including such autos acquired after the policy begins. In Michigan the PIP benefits themselves are added by the Michigan Personal Injury Protection endorsement.
source: ISO CA 00 01 11 20, Section I.A (symbol 5) and I.B.1; ISO Michigan Personal Injury Protection endorsement CA 22 20 (current edition 03 26 per Wolters Kluwer 'Commercial Automobile Policy Forms and Endorsements' list (generated Oct. 13, 2026))

sub: CA Endorsements > Michigan Personal Injury Protection (3107)
q: A Michigan plumbing company insures its vans under the 2020 ISO Business Auto Coverage Form. The Michigan no-fault personal injury protection for the vans is provided by:
choices: Covered Autos Liability Coverage
An Auto Medical Payments Coverage endorsement
The company's workers' compensation policy
A Michigan Personal Injury Protection endorsement
explain: The Business Auto Coverage Form has no PIP section (its sections are Covered Autos, Covered Autos Liability, Physical Damage, Conditions and Definitions). ISO's Michigan Personal Injury Protection endorsement adds the PIP that Michigan's no-fault law requires on Michigan-registered vehicles.
source: ISO CA 00 01 11 20, Sections I–V; ISO Michigan Personal Injury Protection CA 22 20 (03 26 per Wolters Kluwer 'Commercial Automobile Policy Forms and Endorsements' list (generated Oct. 13, 2026)); MCL 500.3101(1), 500.3107; CA 80 04 (Ed. 11/20) Business Auto declarations (PIP 'separately stated in each P.I.P. endorsement')

sub: CA Endorsements > Michigan Property Protection Coverage
q: A Michigan company's van, insured under a Business Auto policy with the Michigan Property Protection Coverage endorsement, slides off a Michigan road and knocks down a homeowner's fence. Which coverage pays for the fence?
choices: Collision Coverage
Property protection insurance (PPI)
Covered Autos Liability Coverage
Comprehensive Coverage
explain: PPI pays, without regard to fault, for accidental damage to tangible property arising out of the use of a motor vehicle in Michigan, up to $1,000,000 per accident. Tort liability for this damage is abolished when the vehicle had the required no-fault security (except for intentionally caused harm), and the van's own physical damage coverages do not pay for the fence.
source: MCL 500.3121(1),(2),(5); MCL 500.3123(2); MCL 500.3135(3); ISO Michigan Property Protection Coverage CA 22 24 (07 21 per Wolters Kluwer 'Commercial Automobile Policy Forms and Endorsements' list (generated Oct. 13, 2026))

q: Under the 2001 ISO Individual Named Insured endorsement, if the individual named insured owns a private passenger auto that is a covered auto for Liability Coverage, the endorsement:
choices: Covers autos owned by employees while used for their personal errands
Adds family members as insureds and covers non-owned autos they or you use
Extends Liability Coverage to autos owned by family members
Covers autos furnished for the named insured's regular use
explain: For an individual named insured, family members become insureds for owned private passenger covered autos, and any auto the named insured does not own is a covered auto while used by the named insured or a family member, with exceptions for family-owned autos, autos furnished for regular use and certain business use. The Fellow Employee Exclusion is lifted only for injury to the named insured's or a family member's fellow employees.
source: ISO CA 99 17 10 01 (Individual Named Insured), A.1, A.2.a–b and C.1

q: Pat, a sole proprietor, has the 2001 ISO Individual Named Insured endorsement on a Business Auto policy, and Pat's own car is a covered auto for Liability Coverage. Which auto is a covered auto for Liability while Pat drives it?
choices: A car owned by Pat's son, who lives with Pat
A car a client furnishes for Pat's regular use
A customer's car Pat drives while working at an auto repair shop
A friend's car Pat borrows for a weekend trip
explain: Any auto Pat does not own is a covered auto while used by Pat or a family member, except autos owned by family members, autos furnished or available for regular use, autos used while working in a business of selling, servicing, repairing or parking autos, and non-private-passenger autos used in any other business.
